title: Choose your platform: legacy Docker vs Kubernetes
breadcrumb: Choose your platform: legacy Docker vs Kubernetes

blocks.html:
Deploy App ships in two stacks that do the same job in very different ways. This page helps you pick the right one and explains the per-page platform toggle you will see across these docs.

TL;DR

  • Running a real deployment today? Use the legacy Docker Compose stack (pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration). It is the production-proven path.
  • Exploring the future / building modular infrastructure on Kubernetes? Use opendefence-platform (pvarki/opendefence-platform). It is alpha and the strategic direction, but not yet the recommended production target.

Not yet documented. A definitive production-readiness status for opendefence-platform is still to be written here. Until then, treat the Kubernetes stack as alpha and don't rely on this page to greenlight a live deployment.

Legacy: Docker Compose

The legacy stack is a set of Docker Compose compositions plus helper scripts that bring the whole system up on a single Docker host.

Use it when:

  • You want the documented, reproducible path that exists today ("zero to running in ~30 minutes").
  • You have a single VM or host and want a self-contained deployment.
  • You need the full product set (TAK, Battlelog, MediaMTX, Matrix) wired together out of the box.

Key mechanics:

  • Components are git submodules of docker-rasenmaeher-integration; you clone with --recurse-submodules and pin a tag for a known-good combination.
  • Certificates and subdomains are handled by miniwerk (pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-miniwerk): Let's Encrypt issuance, the subdomain scheme, and the MW_PRODUCTS variable that lists which products exist.
  • The internal certificate authority is CFSSL (pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-cfssl).
  • Configuration lives in a single .env file at the repo root.
  • You bring it up with docker compose up -d.

See the Operate and Develop Deploy App books for the legacy workflows.

New: Kubernetes (opendefence-platform)

⚠️ Closed alpha — provisional docs. OpenDefence on Kubernetes (opendefence-platform) is in closed alpha and under rapid, breaking development. The Kubernetes content in these docs describes a moving target and will most likely be superseded by the documentation that ships with the first public release — treat everything here as provisional, and do not rely on it for a production deployment.

opendefence-platform converts the legacy compose stack into a Kubernetes-native deployment using Kustomize. It is alpha and modular by design.

Use it when:

  • You are targeting a Kubernetes cluster (local kind for development, or an external cluster for cloud).
  • You want clean separation of infrastructure concerns into operators and per-service folders.
  • You are helping shape the future direction of the platform.

Key mechanics:

  • Each application is split into base/ (environment-agnostic) and overlays/<env>/ (environment-specific: registries, hostnames, certificates, ingress). The overlays in the repo are local and cloud.
  • Tooling is pinned with mise (helm 3, kind 0.31, kubectl 1.36, task 3, yq, zarf). Run mise install and mise trust in the project directory.
  • Common operations run through Taskfile (task up to create a kind cluster and deploy everything, task down to tear it down, task to list tasks).
  • Cloud deployments can be packaged with Zarf (task zarf:package:cloud).
  • The core API runs as deployment/opendefense-rmapi in the opendefense-system namespace.

See Develop Deploy App for the Kubernetes manifests and workflow.

The mechanical differences that matter

Concern Legacy (Docker Compose) New (Kubernetes)
Orchestration docker compose Kustomize manifests applied via task / kubectl
TLS / subdomains miniwerk (Let's Encrypt, MW_PRODUCTS) cert-manager + trust-manager + opendefense-pki
Internal CA CFSSL cert-manager / opendefense-pki
Ingress nginx (driven by miniwerk) Traefik
Component sourcing git submodules per-service base/ + overlays/<env>
Tooling Docker + repo scripts mise-pinned helm/kind/kubectl/task/yq/zarf
Supporting services compose services Kubernetes operators (cloudnative-pg, keycloak-operator, external-secrets-operator, etc.)

miniwerk and CFSSL exist only on the legacy stack. Kustomize, mise, task, and the operators exist only on Kubernetes. These docs do not pretend otherwise.

The per-page platform toggle

Many pages in these docs are scoped to a platform:

  • shared — applies to both stacks (concepts, glossary, user operations).
  • legacy — Docker Compose only.
  • k8s — Kubernetes only.

When a page is platform-specific it carries a toggle so you only read the variant that matches your stack. If you have not decided yet, default to legacy for production and k8s for experimentation, and revisit this page when your needs change.
